description:
## Motivation

The server-sent events parsing algorithm treats CRLF (`\r\n`) as a single
line ending. `EventDataWriter` currently handles every CR and LF independently,
so serializing data such as `first\r\nsecond` inserts an extra `data: ` field
between the CR and LF. Clients consequently decode an unexpected blank line.

The same issue occurs when the CR and LF are written in separate
`fmt::Write::write_str` calls.

## Solution

Track when a write ends with a CR and defer the next `data: ` prefix until the
following byte is known. A following LF completes one CRLF line ending;
otherwise, the CR is handled as a lone line ending. Finalizing the writer also
handles a pending trailing CR.

The `EventDataWriter` documentation now describes CRLF, lone CR, and lone LF
explicitly. Regression tests cover CRLF in one write and every pair of
boundaries that divides mixed line-ending data into three writes.

## Testing

- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features --tests`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p axum --lib --all-features -- -D warnings -A clippy::double_must_use`
- `cargo doc --locked -p axum --all-features --no-deps`
